question_content: A company must use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key to encrypt all Amazon S3 buckets in the company's main AWS Region.The company needs a solution that will detect and remediate any noncompliant S3 buckets. The solution must also notify a security team of any noncompliant S3 buckets. Which solution will meet these requirementswith the LEAST operational effort?

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure the AWS Config managed rule s3-default-encryption-kms. Choose the automatic remediation option. Use AWS Systems Manager Automation documents to publish an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) message to the security team. The security team should turn on AWS KMS encryption for the noncompliant buckets.
answer_choices.solution_content: div class="aws-rationale-content"pIncorrect. You can use AWS Config rules to evaluate AWS resources to ensure that the resources are compliant with specific configuration settings. The s3-default-encryption-kms managed rule would test the buckets for encryption. With the automatic remediation action, noncompliance notifications can pass to the Amazon SNS topic to notify the security team. However, the security team would have to manually turn on encryption for the noncompliant bucket. A better solution would automatically turn on encryption.

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure a Custom AWS Lambda rule in AWS Config to check for AWS KMS encryption on all S3 buckets. Choose the automatic remediation option. Use AWS Systems Manager Automation documents to publish an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) message to the security team. The security team should turn on AWS KMS encryption for the noncompliant buckets.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. You can use AWS Config rules to evaluate AWS resources to ensure that the resources are compliant with specific configuration settings. Amazon SNS can send a notification to the security team. However, a custom AWS Config rule for Lambda is not necessary. An AWS Config managed rule is available. Manual remediation is not the least effort solution. A solution that assigns an automatic remediation script would require less effort.For more information about AWS Config custom rules, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config_develop-rules.html"AWS Config Custom Rules.

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure the AWS Config managed rule s3-default-encryption-kms. Create an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that turns on KMS encryption for the noncompliant buckets and publishes an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) message to the security team. Assign the runbook as automatic remediation for the AWS Config rule.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. You can use AWS Config rules to evaluate AWS resources to ensure that the resources are compliant with specific configuration settings. Amazon SNS can send a notification to the security team. The s3-default-encryption-kms managed rule would test the buckets for encryption. A solution that uses an automatic remediation script to modifies the buckets would require less effort than a solution that uses a manual remediation. For more information about AWS Config rules, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config.html"Evaluating Resources with AWS Config Rules.For more information about the s3-default-encryption-kms rule, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/s3-default-encryption-kms.html"s3-default-encryption-kms.For more information about how to remediate noncompliant AWS resources, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/remediation.html"Remediating Noncompliant AWS Resources by AWS Config Rules.

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure a Custom AWS Lambda rule in AWS Config to check for AWS KMS encryption on all S3 buckets. Create an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that turns on KMS encryption for the noncompliant buckets and publishes an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) message to the security team. Assign the runbook as automatic remediation for the AWS Config rule.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. You can use AWS Config rules to evaluate AWS resources to ensure that the resources are compliant with specific configuration settings. Amazon SNS can send a notification to the security team. A solution that uses an automatic remediation script to modify the buckets would require less effort than a solution that uses manual remediation. However, a custom AWS Config rule for Lambda is not necessary. An AWS Config managed rule that would require less effort is available.For more information about AWS Config custom rules, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config_develop-rules.html"AWS Config Custom Rules.

question_content: A company recognized some unauthorized activities that were performed by using an IAM user's access key. There is a possibility that the IAM user performed malicious activities.What steps should a security team take to reduce the risks?

answer_choices.choice_content: Use the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Access Analyzer to identify the IAM user that is associated with the access key. Deactivate all access keys that are associated with the user. Create a deny all IAM policy. Attach the policy to the user.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. If you deactivate the user's access keys and attach a deny all policy, the user will not have the ability to perform actions on AWS. You can use Access Analyzer to identify AWS resources that are shared with external entities, validate IAM policies, and to generate IAM policies based on AWS CloudTrail activity. However, you cannot use Access Analyzer to identify the IAM user that is associated with the access key credentials. The IAM console can provide the required user information.For more information about Access Analyzer, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/what-is-access-analyzer.html"Using AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Access Analyzer to identify the IAM user that is associated with the access key. Delete the IAM user.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. This solution is not ideal. A better solution would use a policy to prevent the user from taking any additional actions during the investigation of the user. You can remove a policy later rather than delete the IAM user entirely. Additionally, you can use Access Analyzer to identify AWS resources that are shared with external entities, validate IAM policies, and to generate IAM policies based on AWS CloudTrail activity. You cannot use Access Analyzer to identify the IAM user that is associated with the access key credentials. The IAM console can provide the required user information.For more information about Access Analyzer, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/what-is-access-analyzer.html"Using AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) console to identify the IAM user that is associated with the access key.Generate a credential report. Use the data in the credential report to identify the IAM user. Deactivate all access keys that are associated with the user. Create a deny all IAM policy. Attach the policy to the user.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. The IAM console can provide the required user information. You can generate a credential report to locate the user and access key. If you deactivate the user's access keys and attach a deny all policy, the user will not have the ability to perform actions on AWS. If you determine that the breach is accidental, you can generate new access keys and remove the deny all policy. For more information about IAM policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html"Policies and Permissions in IAM.For more information about how to get credential reports, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_getting-report.html#getting-credential-reports-console"Getting Credential Reports (Console).

answer_choices.choice_content: Use the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) console to identify the IAM user that is associated with the access key. Delete the IAM user.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The IAM console can provide the required user information. However, at this point, the breach has not been identified as intentional. In case the breach was accidental, a better solution would use a policy to prevent the user from taking any actions rather than delete the user entirely. You can remove a policy later.For more information about IAM Policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html"Policies and Permissions in IAM.

question_content: A company currently uses an organization in AWS Organizations to manage the company's AWS accounts. The company collects logs for the accounts from a number of sources, including VPC flow logs, AWS CloudTrail log files, and DNS logs. The company wants to implement an automated solution to detect anomalous activity in the AWS accounts.The automated solution must analyze the logs for common forms of suspicious activity. A security team must receive notifications for any findings.Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

answer_choices.choice_content: Use an Amazon CloudWatch Logs subscription to send log data to an Amazon S3 bucket in the organization's management account. Use Amazon Athena queries to analyze the log data for suspicious activity. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to subscribe to findings of suspicious activity.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. An S3 bucket is not a valid target for a CloudWatch Logs subscription. Athena is an interactive query service that can analyze data in Amazon S3 by using standard SQL. A solution that writes queries to detect suspicious activity would be time consuming. This solution would not be as effective as a more sophisticated and managed solution. Amazon SNS can receive notifications from Amazon EventBridge about the status of Athena queries (such as success or failure). These notifications would not contain any information about whether the queries detected suspicious activity.For more information about CloudWatch Logs subscription filters, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/SubscriptionFilters.html"Using CloudWatch Logs Subscription Filters.For more information about Athena, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/when-should-i-use-ate.html"When Should I Use Athena?For more information about the use of Athena with EventBridge, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/query-metrics-viewing.html"Monitoring Athena Queries with CloudWatch Metrics.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use an Amazon CloudWatch Logs subscription to send log data to an AWS Lambda function in the security team’s account. Use the function to analyze the log data for suspicious activity. Use Amazon CloudWatch Events to subscribe to findings of suspicious activity.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. You can configure CloudWatch Logs with a subscription filter to send log data to Amazon Kinesis or Lambda. Lambda is not an appropriate service to use in this scenario. A single function is unlikely to be able to handle the volume of logs being sent from the log stream. Each log stream would activate a separate Lambda function. It is not clear how Lambda would effectively analyze these data for suspicious activity. As well as being overly complex, this configuration is unlikely to generate any meaningful results.For more information about CloudWatch Logs subscription filters, se href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/SubscriptionFilters.html"Using CloudWatch Logs Subscription Filters.

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure Amazon GuardDuty for the organization. Designate the security team’s account as a delegated administrator. Use Amazon CloudWatch Events to subscribe to findings of suspicious activity.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. GuardDuty is a continuous security monitoring service that analyzes and processes multiple data sources. GuardDuty creates an event for CloudWatch Events when any change in findings takes place. Finding changes that will create an event include newly generated findings or newly aggregated findings. This solution meets the requirements efficiently, with minimal operational effort.For more information about GuardDuty, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/what-is-guardduty.html"What Is Amazon GuardDuty?For more information about the use of CloudWatch Events with GuardDuty, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_findings_cloudwatch.html"Creating Custom Responses to GuardDuty Findings with Amazon CloudWatch Events.For more information about how GuardDuty uses data sources, se href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_data-sources.html"How Amazon GuardDuty Uses Its Data Sources.

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure Amazon GuardDuty for the organization. Designate the security team’s account as a delegated administrator. Configure GuardDuty to synchronize the logs from the organization's AWS accounts to an S3 bucket for analysis. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to subscribe to findings of suspicious activity.
answer_choices.solution_content: div class="aws-rationale-content"pIncorrect. GuardDuty is a continuous security monitoring service that analyzes and processes multiple data sources. GuardDuty creates an event for CloudWatch Events when any change in findings takes place. Finding changes that will create an event include newly generated findings or newly aggregated findings. Amazon SNS can receive notifications from GuardDuty about the status of queries (such as success or failure). However, these notifications would not contain any information about whether the query detected suspicious activity. GuardDuty does not need to and cannot explicitly copy logs from other AWS accounts to conduct analysis and generate findings.

question_content: A company has many Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes that are spread across the company's fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. A security consultant must develop an automated solution to scan the EBS volumes for malware. The solution must also log potential malware that the scans find.pThe security consultant creates an Amazon EventBridge rule and sets an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group as the target for the rule.pWhat should the security consultant do next to meet these requirements?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: Turn on Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection. Configure the EventBridge rule to match a GuardDuty finding when the finding type is Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile or Execution:EC2/SuspiciousFile.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. To scan EC2 instances and EBS volumes for malware, the security consultant must turn on Malware Protection within the GuardDuty console. The GuardDuty finding types that specifically relate to an EC2 instance or EBS volume finding are Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile and Execution:EC2/SuspiciousFile. For more information about Malware Protection finding types, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/findings-malware-protection.html"Malware Protection Finding Types.For more information about Malware Protection, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/malware-protection.html"Malware Protection in Amazon GuardDuty.

answer_choices.choice_content: Turn on Amazon EC2 Malware Protection. Configure the EventBridge rule to match an EBS volume notification when the finding type is PACKAGE_VULNERABILITY.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Amazon EC2 does not have a feature named Malware Protection. Additionally, EBS volume notifications do not have finding types. Amazon EBS can send events to EventBridge. However, these events are not related to malware detection. Amazon EBS events are about actions taken against an EBS volume, including createVolume, deleteVolume, and attachVolume. For more information about Amazon EBS events that you can send to EventBridge, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-cloud-watch-events.html"EventBridge for Amazon EBS.

answer_choices.choice_content: Turn on Amazon Inspector Malware Protection. Configure the EventBridge rule to match an Amazon Inspector finding when the finding type is Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile or Execution:EC2/SuspiciousFile.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Amazon Inspector does not have a feature named Malware Protection. You can use Amazon Inspector to reveal software and network vulnerabilities in AWS resources. The vulnerabilities could lead to exposure to malware for resources like EC2 instances and container images. However, Amazon Inspector does not scan for the presence of malware itself. Additionally, Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile and Execution:EC2/SuspiciousFile are finding types for GuardDuty, not Amazon Inspector. Amazon Inspector's finding types are PACKAGE_VULNERABILITY and NEWORK_REACHABILITY.For more information about Amazon Inspector, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/what-is-inspector.html"What Is Amazon Inspector?a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/what-is-inspector.html"/aFor more information about Amazon Inspector finding types, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/findings-types.html"Finding Types in Amazon Inspector.

answer_choices.choice_content: Turn on Amazon EBS Malware Protection. Configure the EventBridge rule to match an EBS volume notification when the finding type is PACKAGE_VULNERABILITY.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Amazon EBS does not have a feature named Malware Protection. Amazon EBS can send events to EventBridge. However, these events are not related to malware detection. Amazon EBS events are about actions taken against an EBS volume, including createVolume, deleteVolume, and attachVolume.For more information about Amazon EBS events that you can send to EventBridge, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-cloud-watch-events.html"EventBridge for Amazon EBS.

question_content: A company uses AWS Control Tower to organize its various accounts. A security team uses Amazon GuardDuty to continuously monitor its AWS resources. The security team must design an automated detection and remediation process for security findings such as Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile. The process should gather forensics on the Amazon EC2 instance to understand the findings more completely. All the EC2 instances run in Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content:
Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect findings such as Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile. Set up an Amazon Simple Notification Service 
  (Amazon SNS) topic with aws-controltower-SecurityNotifications as a target. Create subscriptions to this topic with the email address of the security team. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to terminate the instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The aws-controltower-SecurityNotifications topic automatically receives security notification messages without the need for an EventBridge rule. Automatic termination of the instance would not meet the requirement to collect forensics.For more information about AWS Control Tower notifications, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/receive-notifications.html"Compliance Notifications by SNS in the Audit Account.For more information about infrastructure domain incidents, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-security-incident-response-guide/infrastructure-domain-incidents.html"AWS Security Incident Response Guide.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect findings such as Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile. Set up an AWS Lambda function as a target to capture metadata on the instance. Turn on termination protection. Isolate the instance by switching to a fully restrictive security group. Detach the instance from any Auto Scaling groups. Deregister from any load balancers. Snapshot all volumes. Quarantine the instance for investigation.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. EventBridge can receive events whenever GuardDuty produces findings. An EventBridge rule can detect a specific GuardDuty finding such as Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile. An EventBridge rule can invoke a Lambda function. This solution follows the recommendations of the AWS Incident Response Guide.For more information about AWS security incident response recommendations, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-security-incident-response-guide/infrastructure-domain-incidents.html"AWS Security Incident Response Guide.For more information about GuardDuty findings and EventBridge, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_findings_cloudwatch.html"Creating Custom Responses to GuardDuty Findings with Amazon EventBridge.For more information about the GuardDuty Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile finding, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/findings-malware-protection.html#execution-malware-ec2-maliciousfile"Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile.

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure Amazon Detective to respond to findings such as Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile. Configure Detective to capture metadata on the instance. Turn on termination protection. Isolate the instance by switching to a fully restrictive security group. Detach the instance from any Auto Scaling groups. Deregister from any load balancers. Snapshot all volumes. Quarantine the instance for investigation.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Detective automatically processes terabytes of event data records to analyze, investigate, and quickly identify the root cause of security findings or suspicious activities. However, Detective cannot perform actions against an EC2 instance.For more information about Detective, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/detective/latest/adminguide/what-is-detective.html"What Is Amazon Detective?

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure Amazon Detective to respond to findings such as Execution:EC2/MaliciousFile. Configure Detective to capture metadata on the instance. Isolate the instance by switching to a fully restrictive security group. Detach the instance from any Auto Scaling groups. Deregister from any load balancers. Snapshot all volumes. Terminate the instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Detective automatically processes terabytes of event data records to analyze, investigate, and quickly identify the root cause of security findings or suspicious activities. However, Detective cannot perform actions against an EC2 instance. Also, you should not terminate the instance.For more information about Detective, seespan style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/detective/latest/adminguide/what-is-detective.html"What Is Amazon Detective?

question_content: A security engineer discovered a vulnerability in an application running on Amazon ECS. The vulnerability allowed attackers to install malicious code. Analysis of the code shows it exfiltrates data on port 5353 in batches at random time intervals.While the code of the containers is being patched, how can engineers quickly identify all compromised hosts and stop the egress of data on port 5353?

answer_choices.choice_content: Enable AWS Shield Advanced and AWS WAF. Configure an AWS WAF custom filter for egress traffic on port 5353.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Shield Advanced is designed to detect and mitigate DDoS attacks. Shield Advanced is not able to run vulnerability scans on your applications. Additionally, AWS WAF is a service that works at the application layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model. You cannot use an AWS WAF custom filter to filter port traffic.For more information about how to filter AWS WAF, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-get-started-web-acl-rbr.html"Configure Application Layer (Layer 7) DDoS Protections with AWS WAF. For more information about Shield Advanced, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-advanced-summary.html"AWS Shield Advanced Overview.

answer_choices.choice_content: Enable Amazon Inspector on Amazon ECS and configure a custom assessment to evaluate containers that have port 5353 open. Update the NACLs to block port 5353 outbound.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Amazon Inspector only performs package vulnerability scans on container images, which do not include egress access on a specific port. To scan the network for instances where the port is open, the engineers would have to run the Network Reachability package from Amazon Inspector to identify open ports. To get additional information about processes that run on the port, engineers would have to install the Amazon Inspector agent.For more information about how to use Amazon Inspector to scan resources, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/scanning-resources.html"Scanning Resources with Amazon Inspector.For more information about how to use Amazon Inspector to scan container images, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/scanning-ecr.html"Scanning Amazon ECR Container Images with Amazon Inspector.For more information about Amazon Inspector findings, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/findings-types.html"Finding Types in Amazon Inspector.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an Amazon CloudWatch custom metric on the VPC Flow Logs identifying egress traffic on port 5353. Update the NACLs to block port 5353 outbound.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. VPC Flow logs allow you to collect a log record of traffic that flows between network interfaces in a VPC. VPC Flow logs can be published to CloudWatch, which allows you to run queries and discover any egress traffic through port 5353. If egress traffic is discovered over port 5353, you can create or update the NACL where the application resides to block outbound traffic over port 5353.For more information about VPC Flow logs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html"Logging IP Traffic Using VPC Flow Logs.For more information about how to publish to CloudWatch Logs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs-cwl.html"Publish Flow Logs to CloudWatch Logs.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use Amazon Athena to query AWS CloudTrail logs in Amazon S3 and look for any traffic on port 5353. Update the security groups to block port 5353 outbound.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Although you can use Athena to query CloudTrail logs, CloudTrail logs do not contain traffic port information. For traffic port information, you need to use VPC Flow Logs. Security Groups cannot create rules to explicitly deny traffic from port 5353. Instead, you could create a NACL with rules to block outbound traffic.For more information about Security Group rules, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/security-groups.html"Security Groups.For more information about CloudTrail logs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-event-reference-record-contents.html"CloudTrail Record Contents.For more information about VPC Flow logs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html"Logging IP Traffic Using VPC Flow Logs.

question_content:
The InfoSec team has mandated that in the future only approved Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) can be used./p
How can the InfoSec team ensure compliance with this mandate?/div

answer_choices.choice_content: Terminate all Amazon EC2 instances and relaunch them with approved AMIs.
answer_choices.solution_content: div class="aws-rationale-content"pIncorrect. This a manual action to remediate the problem, and there is no way to enforce the approved AMIs. To enforce approved AMIs, the team should use an AWS Config rule to enforce compliance.

answer_choices.choice_content: Patch all running instances by using AWS Systems Manager.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Although patching the AMIs with Systems Manager could provide intended compliance, the AMIs could still be out of compliance with the Info Sec team based on the specific approved AMIs or AMI versions. Patching does not replace the AMIs. Patching only maintains APIs.For more information about Systems Manager patching, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-patch.html"AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager.

answer_choices.choice_content: Deploy AWS Config rules and check all running instances for compliance.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. There is a managed Config rule that verifies whether you use approved instances. This Config rule can be used to enforce compliance.For more information about how to enforce approved AMIs, seespan style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/approved-amis-by-id.html"approved-amis-by-id.

answer_choices.choice_content: Define a metric filter in Amazon CloudWatch Logs to verify compliance.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. CloudWatch Logs allow you to create and collect records of events. If you create a metric filter in CloudWatch Logs, you can filter through logs and determine if unapproved AMIs are being used. However, filtering logs does not actually prevent the usage of unapproved AMIs. If you want to ensure that approved AMIs are used, you can use an AWS Config rule to enforce compliance.For more information about how to use metric filter in CloudWatch Logs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/MonitoringLogData.html"Creating Metrics from Log Events Using Filters.

question_content: After multiple compromises of its Amazon EC2 instances, a company's security officer is mandating that memory dumps of compromised instances be captured for further analysis. A security engineer just received an EC2 abuse notification report from AWS stating that an EC2 instance running the most recent Windows Server 2019 Base AMI is compromised.How should the security engineer collect a memory dump of the EC2 instance for forensic analysis?

answer_choices.choice_content: Give consent to the AWS Security team to dump the memory core on the compromised instance and provide it to AWS Support for analysis.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The security pillar in the AWS shared responsibility model states that a user is responsible for “Security in the cloud.” This means that AWS support does not perform tasks like collecting memory dump files, because this is considered part of the user's responsibility.For more information about the security pillar in the AWS shared responsibility model, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/shared-responsibility.html"Shared Responsibility.

answer_choices.choice_content: Review memory dump data that the AWS Systems Manager Agent sent to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) is software that specifically makes it possible for the AWS Systems Manager service to manage and update EC2 instances. The agent does not interact with memory dumps. SSM Agent processes requests from the Systems Manager service in the cloud, and runs them on the EC2 instance.For more information about SSM Agent, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/ssm-agent.html"Working with SSM Agent.

answer_choices.choice_content: Download and run the EC2Rescue for Windows Server utility from AWS.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. EC2Rescue for Windows Server can capture memory-dump files that exist on the EC2 instance. EC2Rescue for Windows Server can also capture EC2 instance event logs, configuration logs, and SSM Agent logs. EC2 Rescue for Windows Server can be downloaded from AWS and run manually, or accessed through an AWS Systems Manager run command document.For more information about EC2Rescue for Windows, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/WindowsGuide/Windows-Server-EC2Rescue.html"Use EC2Rescue for Windows Server.

answer_choices.choice_content: Reboot the EC2 Windows Server, enter safe mode, and select memory dump.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The reboot of an EC2 instance erases the RAM. Therefore, rebooting would lose the EC2 instance state that you are trying to capture.For more information about the instance lifecycle, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-lifecycle.html#lifecycle-differences"Differences Between Reboot, Stop, Hibernate, and Terminate.

question_content: The access key of an IAM user within a company is compromised. The company discovers that multiple new Amazon EC2 instances have been launched unexpectedly. A security engineer must immediately minimize the impact. Additionally, the affected resources must be isolated for offline forensic analysis.pWhich combination of actions should the security engineer take, based on AWS recommendations? (Select THREE.)/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: Use SSH to access the new instances. Copy all logs to an Amazon S3 bucket. Terminate the instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. It is possible to have SSH access to the new instances and to copy all the logs, such as system logs, to an S3 bucket. However, manual interaction with the operating system is not a best practice. question_content: A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The company also has an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that is protected by a web ACL. You can use the access logs to analyze traffic patterns and troubleshoot issues. Amazon Athena can run interactive queries against data directly in Amazon S3 without the need to format data or manage infrastructure. Athena is appropriate to run a query on logs for this scenario. However, a solution that adds the identified IP address to the load balancer's listener rules is not scalable. Load balancers allow up to a maximum of 100 listener rules, which is not sufficient to block traffic at this scale.For more information about Amazon Athena, see a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/what-is.html"span style="text-decoration: underline;"What Is Amazon Athena?/span/aFor more information about Elastic Load Balancer logs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-access-logs.html"Access Logs for Your Application Load Balancer.For more information about Elastic Load Balancer quotas, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-limits.html"Quotas for Your Application Load Balancers.

question_content: A company plans to create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with two origin servers. Both origins are Amazon S3 buckets, named DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET1 and DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET2. Some AWS resources need read access to the objects in DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET1. Only the CloudFront distribution needs access to the objects that are in both buckets.pA security administrator must implement a solution to restrict access to the S3 buckets.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?/p/div

The bucket policy for DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET2 should allow read access to the CloudFront distribution only.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a bucket policy in DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET1to allow read access to the CloudFront distribution and the appropriate AWS resources. Create a CloudFront origin access control (OAC) to associate with the CloudFront distribution. Create a bucket policy in DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET2 to allow read access to the OAC only.
answer_choices.solution_content: div class="aws-rationale-content"pIncorrect. You cannot list a CloudFront distribution as a principal in an IAM resource-based policy. A CloudFront OAC, a special CloudFront user, allows a CloudFront distribution to access to an S3 bucket.

Create a bucket policy for DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET1to allow read access to the appropriate AWS resources and the OAC. Create a bucket policy for DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET2 to allow read access only to the OAC.

question_content: A company hosts a website on Amazon EC2 instances that run behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to serve all types of users. To protect some private content and minimize load on the EC2 instances, the company wants to filter out unauthorized requests based on a JSON Web Token (JWT) in the query string of a request.Which solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create and associate a CloudFront function to the CloudFront distribution that has the viewer request event type. Use the function to validate the JWT value.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. CloudFront functions are deployed at the edge location. You can associate CloudFront functions at the viewer request stage, where the functions will evaluate requests before processing. In this scenario, the function can validate the JWT value to prevent unauthorized requests from being processed further at the edge location.For more information about CloudFront functions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/cloudfront-functions.html"Customizing at the Edge with CloudFront Functions.For more information about how to associate CloudFront functions with CloudFront distributions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/associate-function.html"Associating Functions with Distributions.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create and associate a WAF web ACL to the CloudFront distribution. Add a custom rule for the web ACL to match a query string with the JWT value.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A WAF is a web application firewall that protects AWS resources against common web exploits and bots that can affect availability, compromise security, or consume excessive resources. A web ACL inspects and handles web requests based on the defined criteria. You can define a custom rule to filter requests based on the content of headers. However, the custom rule cannot process the content further. In this case, the request can be filtered based on the presence of JWT query string or header. The custom rule cannot process and validate the JWT value itself.For more information about WAF, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/how-aws-waf-works.html"How AWS WAF Works.For more information about WAF rules, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rules.html"Rules.For more information about the components of web requests in WAF, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-fields-list.html"Request Component Options.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create and associate an AWS Lambda@Edge function to the CloudFront distribution that has the origin request event type. Use the function to validate the JWT value.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. You deploy Lambda@Edge functions at the Regional edge caches. Lambda@Edge can process the events at different stages of the request. However, in this scenario, the function evaluates the request for a valid JWT value before the function forwards the request to the origin. If a request is made for the private content and the response is available through the CloudFront distribution, the distribution might serve the private content without any authorization. This solution does not protect the private content from unauthorized requests.For more information about Lambda@Edge, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/lambda-at-the-edge.html"Customizing at the Edge with Lambda@Edge.For more information about CloudFront, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/HowCloudFrontWorks.html"How CloudFront Delivers Content.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a listener rule that has an authenticate action on the load balancer. Validate the JWT value that is defined in the x-amzn-oidc-data field of the request’s user claims.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. An ALB facilitates secure authentication of users as the users access applications. This feature offloads the work of user authentication to the load balancer. This process requires additional configuration of authentication flow with identity providers. However, if a request is made to the CloudFront distribution for the private content and the response is available, the distribution might serve the private content without any authorization. This solution does not protect the private content from unauthorized requests. The requests must be validated at the edge.For more information about user authentication with ALBs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/listener-authenticate-users.html"Authenticate Users Using an Application Load Balancer.For more information about CloudFront, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/HowCloudFrontWorks.html"How CloudFront Delivers Content.

question_content: A company has a prototype three-tier application architecture on AWS. Each tier consists of Amazon EC2 instances in EC2 Auto Scaling groups.The first tier (web tier) is in a public subnet named SubnetA and has a security group named WebSG. WebSG allows incoming traffic from the internet on Port 443.The second tier (application tier) is in a private subnet named SubnetB and has a security group named AppSG. AppSG allows incoming traffic from the WebSG on Port 80.The third tier (database tier) is in a private subnet named subnetC and has a security group named DBSG. DBSG allows incoming traffic from the AppSG on Port 1521.The company recently discovered that the second tier was unintentionally communicating with another EC2 instance in a peered VPC. The company would like to prevent this communication in the future.Which solution will meet this requirement?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a network ACL that has an inbound rule that allows traffic from the instances in the application tier to communicate with the database tier and that denies all other traffic. Attach the network ACL to SubnetC.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Network ACLs can restrict the traffic between the application tier and the database tier. However, network ACL rules are stateless. Therefore, you would need to create both an inbound and outbound rule to allow the proper communication.For more information about network ACLs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html"Control Traffic to Subnets Using Network ACLs.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a network ACL that has an outbound rule that allows traffic from the instances in the application tier to communicate with the database tier and denies all other traffic. Attach the network ACL to SubnetB.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Network ACLs can restrict the traffic between the application tier and the database tier. However, network ACL rules are stateless. Therefore, you would need to create both an inbound and outbound rule to allow the proper communication.For more information about network ACLs, seespan style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html"Control Traffic to Subnets Using Network ACLs.

answer_choices.choice_content: Add an outbound rule to AppSG to allow only traffic on Port 1521 that is destined for the IP subnet of the database instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. Security groups act as virtual firewalls to control traffic that is allowed to reach and leave the resource security groups are associated with. A modification to the default outbound rule that allows only outbound traffic to Port 1521 in the database server subnet would prevent communication with other resources and protocols.For more information about security groups, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_SecurityGroups.html"Control Traffic to Resources Using Security Groups.

answer_choices.choice_content: Add an outbound rule to AppSG to deny only traffic on Port 1521.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Security groups act as virtual firewalls to control traffic that is allowed to reach and leave the resource the security groups are associated with. However, security groups do not support deny rules. To restrict the communication, you must replace the default outbound rule with a rule that will allow only outbound traffic to Port 1521 in the database server's subnet. Although you can use another security group as a source when you build security groups, the destination addresses must be in CIDR format.For more information about security groups, seespan style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_SecurityGroups.html"Control Traffic to Resources Using Security Groups.

question_content: A company runs multiple mission-critical web applications on Amazon EC2 instances in an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. A security team would like to inspect the content of all traffic that involves these EC2 instances. Due to strict latency requirements in the SLA, the team wants to perform this inspection passively. The team does not want to affect network performance.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: Use VPC Flow Logs with a custom log record format and Amazon Athena to analyze the flow logs.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. VPC Flow Logs captures information about the IP traffic to and from network interfaces in a VPC. Flow log data can be published to Amazon CloudWatch Logs or Amazon S3. However, flow logs do not capture the message content for content inspection.For more information about VPC Flow Logs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html"Logging IP Traffic Using VPC Flow Logs.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use VPC Traffic Mirroring and a Gateway Load Balancer with security appliances to analyze the traffic.
answer_choices.solution_content:
div class="aws-rationale-content"
	pCorrect. Traffic Mirroring copies traffic to and from the network interfaces to monitoring appliances. In this scenario, the original packets from all network interfaces that are attached to the EC2 instances can be mirrored to the Gateway Load Balancer. The load balancer can distribute the packets to the security appliance that run on EC2 instances for deep-packet (content) inspection. Because of this out-of-band traffic inspection, the EC2 instances that run the web applications will not have any impact on network performance./p

	pFor more information about Traffic Mirroring, seespan style="text-decoration: underline;"a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/what-is-traffic-mirroring.html" target="_blank"What Is Traffic Mirroring?/p

	pFor more information about Traffic Mirroring concepts, see span style="text-decoration: underline;"a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/traffic-mirroring-how-it-works.html" target="_blank"How Traffic Mirroring Works.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use VPC internet gateway route tables and the network interface of a security appliance to analyze the traffic.
answer_choices.solution_content:
div class="aws-rationale-content"
	pIncorrect. You can associate a gateway route table with an internet gateway or a virtual private gateway. The route table forwards all incoming traffic from the internet gateway to a security appliance before the traffic reaches the EC2 instances that run the web application. You can use the security appliance for deep-packet (content) inspection. However, this is an active inline traffic inspection technique, not a passive technique. This solution would affect the overall network performance of the web applications./p

	pFor more information about gateway route tables, see span style="text-decoration: underline;"a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Route_Tables.html#gateway-route-tables" target="_blank"Gateway Route Tables./p

	pFor more information about how to inspect traffic to a subnet, see span style="text-decoration: underline;"a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/internet-gateway-subnet.html" target="_blank"Inspect Traffic Destined for a Subnet./p

	pFor more information about Traffic Mirroring, seespan style="text-decoration: underline;"a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/what-is-traffic-mirroring.html" target="_blank"What Is Traffic Mirroring?

answer_choices.choice_content: Use VPC internet gateway route tables and a Gateway Load Balancer with security appliances to analyze the traffic.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. You can associate a gateway route table with an internet gateway or a virtual private gateway. The route table forwards all incoming traffic from the internet gateway to the Gateway Load Balancer. A Gateway Load Balancer can redirect traffic to a fleet of security appliances before the traffic reaches the EC2 instances that run the web application. You can use the security appliance for deep-packet (content) inspection. However, this is an active inline traffic inspection technique, not a passive technique. This solution would affect the overall network performance of the web applications.For more information about gateway route tables, se href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Route_Tables.html#gateway-route-tables"Gateway Route Tables.For more information about security appliances behind a Gateway Load Balancer, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/gwlb-route.html"Inspect Traffic Using Appliances in a Security VPC.

question_content: A company usedAmazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to deploy an application in the private subnets of the EKS cluster VPC across multiple Availability Zones. The company configured the application to use the public internet to connect to an AWS Partner’s custom database solution on TCP/IP Port 27017. The AWS Partner hosts the database solution in a VPC that is in a separate AWS account.A DevOps engineer must secure the application by ensuring that connections to the database do not leave the AWS network. These connections must be accessible only from the EKS cluster pods. The traffic across these two VPCs must be restricted to database connections only. The AWS Partner offers both AWS PrivateLink and VPC peering options. The AWS Partner provides a VPC IPv4 CIDR range and an endpoint service name for further configuration.Which solutions will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an interface VPC endpoint for the provided endpoint service within the EKS cluster VPC. Assign a security group to the interface endpoint that allows inbound connections from the AWS Partner’s database and outbound connections to 0.0.0.0/0 on Port 27017. Update the EKS pod security group to allow inbound connections from the interface endpoint on Port 27017.
answer_choices.solution_content: div class="aws-rationale-content"pIncorrect. When you use PrivateLink, VPC endpoints can make private connections from a VPC to supported AWS services, services that other AWS accounts host (VPC endpoint services), and supported AWS Marketplace partner services. The application that runs in EKS pods must initialize connections to the database. However, the pod security group and the security group that is attached to the interface endpoint allow inbound traffic, instead of outbound traffic, to initialize the database connection. Because of the security group's incorrect configurations, this solution will not work.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a VPC peering connection between the EKS cluster VPC and the AWS Partner’s VPC. Update the EKS VPC route tables to allow inbound connections only from the database security group. Update the EKS pod security group to allow outbound connections to the peered VPC CIDR range on Port 27017.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A VPC peering connection gives two VPCs the ability to route traffic between one another. These connections use private IPv4 addresses or IPv6 addresses.The traffic does not leave the AWS network. With a peering connection, VPC route tables can provide access the entire VPC CIDR block, a specific part of the VPC CIDR block, or a specific instance within the peer VPC. However, VPC route tables cannot use security groups to route traffic. Additionally, VPC peering provides bidirectional network access between two VPCs. This solution unnecessarily gives the AWS Partner's VPC the ability to access to the EKS cluster VPC resources. Because of the incorrect VPC peering configuration, this solution will not work.For more information about VPC peering, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/vpc-peering-basics.html"VPC Peering Basics.For more information about VPC peering with specific routes, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/peering-configurations-partial-access.html"VPC Peering Configurations with Specific Routes.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a PrivateLink interface endpoint for the provided endpoint service within the EKS cluster VPC. Assign a security group to the interface endpoint that allows inbound connections from the EKS pod security group. Update the EKS pod security group to allow outbound connections to the interface endpoint on Port 27017.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. When you use PrivateLink, VPC endpoints can make private connections from a VPC to supported AWS services, services that other AWS accounts host (VPC endpoint services), and PrivateLink Ready partners. PrivateLink connections have unidirectional access only. In this scenario, the EKS cluster VPC resources must initialize the database connection to the endpoint service. The endpoint service cannot initialize the database connection to the EKS cluster VPC resources. The pod security group makes the database connection possible only through the interface endpoint. Lastly, the interface endpoint’s security group is restricted to allow incoming connections only from the pod security group. Overall, this restrictive traffic access meets the requirements.For more information about PrivateLink, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/endpoint-services-overview.html"Connect Your VPC to Services Using AWS PrivateLink.For more information about interface endpoints, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpce-interface.html"Access an AWS Service Using an Interface VPC Endpoint.For more information about security groups in Amazon EKS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/sec-group-reqs.html"Amazon EKS Security Group Requirements and Considerations.For more information about security groups, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_SecurityGroups.html"Control Traffic to Resources Using Security Groups.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a VPC peering connection between the EKS cluster VPC and the AWS Partner’s VPC. Update the EKS VPC route tables to allow inbound connections from AWS Partner’s VPC CIDR range. Update the EKS pod security group to allow outbound connections to the AWS Partner’s VPC CIDR range on Port 27017.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A VPC peering connection provides bidirectional network access between two VPCs without leaving the AWS network. The AWS Partner's VPC does not need access to the EKS VPC, so this configuration does not meet the requirement to allow only database connections.For more information about VPC Peering, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/vpc-peering-basics.html"VPC Peering Basics.

question_content: A company has a large deployment of Amazon EC2 instances in its VPC. The VPC has an Amazon S3 endpoint configured. Trusted Advisor does not give data on operating system patches installed on EC2 instances. Although Trusted Advisor cannot be used to create a list of required patches for each instance, Systems Manager Run Command is the right solution to apply patches in the list. Systems Manager Run Commands are used to run configuration changes on managed instances. In this scenario, the configuration change to apply a patch.For more information about Trusted Advisor, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/trusted-advisor.html"AWS Trusted Advisor.

question_content: A company deployed a proof-of-concept three-tier application. The company deployed each tier on a separate Amazon EC2 instance. You must configure both inbound and outbound rules separately to allow bidirectional communication of the resources that are deployed in different subnets. For an incoming request, the database will use an ephemeral port to respond. The outbound rule for N1 allows this required communication from the database to the application. The resolution of these two issues should make successful communication possible without timeout errors.For more information about security groups, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_SecurityGroups.html"Control Traffic to Resources Using Security Groups.For more information about network ACLs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html"Control Traffic to Subnets Using Network ACLs.

A new network ACL is a custom network ACL. A custom network ACL denies all inbound and outbound traffic until you add appropriate rules. You must configure both inbound and outbound rules separately to allow bidirectional communication of the resources that are deployed in different subnets. For an incoming request, the database will use an ephemeral port to respond. The outbound rule for N1 allows this required communication from the database to the application. question_content: A company is using an external CI/CD system to create and manage resources in an AWS account. This CI/CD system uses the access key of an IAM user. An IAM policy that has appropriate permissions is attached directly to the IAM user. The company previously experienced a security breach that resulted in the public exposure of credentials. The security breach was more severe because of infrequent access key rotation.pRecently, the company implemented an external identity provider (IdP) that supports OpenID Connect (OIDC). The company has contracted a security engineer to create a secure authentication solution that uses the external IdP.pWhich solution will meet these requirements MOST securely?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: Use the external IdP URL to create an IAM OIDC identity provider. Register the CI/CD system as an audience to the external IdP. Add the CI/CD system's clientID to the IAM OIDC identity provider. Assign a new IAM role that has the appropriate permissions to the external IdP. Configure the CI/CD system to assume the role by using the AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity action.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. An IAM OIDC identity provider establishes a trust relationship between an OIDC-compatible IdP and an AWS account for federation of external identities. You use the external IdP URL to configure an IAM OIDC identity provider. In this scenario, the CI/CD system, which is registered to the external IdP, can access the AWS account as a federated user. The CI/CD system uses the IAM role that is assigned to the external IdP. IAM roles provide temporary security credentials (temporary access keys) dynamically with each role session. By default, a role session lasts for 1 hour. The temporary credentials eliminate the need to create and maintain long-term access keys for IAM users. With successful authentication and dynamic usage of short-term keys, this solution is the most secure option.For more information about how to create OIDC identity providers, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_providers_create_oidc.html"Creating OpenID Connect (OIDC) Identity Providers.For more information about how to request temporary credentials, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_temp_request.html"Requesting Temporary Security Credentials.

answer_choices.choice_content: Remove the existing IAM policy that is attached directly to the IAM user. Create a new IAM role that has a trust policy that restricts the AssumeRole action to the user. Attach the existing IAM policy to the role. Configure the CI/CD system to assume the role by using the access keys that are associated with the user. Rotate the access keys for the IAM user every day.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. IAM roles provide temporary security credentials dynamically for each role session. IAM roles do improve the security in this scenario. However, the existing IAM user's static access keys assume this role. Despite the daily rotation of this access key, the access key can be breached. A breach would result in exposure for an entire day. This solution is not the most secure option. A better solution would provide access dynamically with a more restricted time limit.For more information about IAM roles, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles.html"IAM Roles.For more information about the management of access keys, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/accounts/latest/reference/credentials-access-keys-best-practices.html"Best Practices for Managing AWS Access Keys.For more information about AWS account access, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html"AWS Security Credentials.

Configure the CI/CD system to assume the role by using the AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity action.

This process will use temporary security credentials rather than long-term access keys. This process uses the IAM role and provides a secure solution. This solution is not a correct configuration.For more information about how to create OIDC Providers, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_providers_create_oidc.html"Creating OpenID Connect (OIDC) Identity Providers.

question_content: A company uses Microsoft Active Directory for access management for on-premises resources and wants to use the same mechanism for accessing its AWS accounts. question_content: Multiple IAM users programmatically assume an IAM role. This role has an IAM policy attached that provides full access to Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS resources. Session policies limit the permissions from the role or user's IAM policy that are assigned to the session. Session policies do not grant any additional permissions. The session's permissions are a result of the interaction between the IAM policies for the IAM entity (user or role) and the session policy. A session policy that allows access to only S3 resources will prevent access to EC2 and RDS resources during the session. With this solution, User1 cannot access S3 resources because the IAM role does not have permissions to access S3 resources.For more information about session policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html#policies_session"Session Policies.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a new IAM role that grants full access to S3, EC2, and RDS resources. Direct User1 to assume this new role instead of the existing role.

A new IAM role that has all the required access for User1 will meet the requirements.For more information about identity-based policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html#policies_id-based"Identity-Based Policies.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a session policy that grants full access to S3, EC2, and RDS resources. Include the session policy as a parameter when User1 assumes the existing role.

Session policies limit the permissions from the role or user's IAM policy that are assigned to the session. Session policies do not grant any additional permissions. The session's permissions are a result of the interaction between the IAM policies for the IAM entity (user or role) and the session policy. The session policy in this solution provides access to EC2 and RDS resources during the session. However, User1 cannot access S3 resources because the IAM role does not have permissions to access S3 resources.For more information about session policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html#policies_session"Session Policies.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an IAM policy that grants full access to S3 resources. Attach the new policy directly to User1. Direct User1 to assume the existing role.

However, when User1 assumes the existing role, only the permissions that are associated specifically with the role are in effect. User1 would not have the required access to S3 resources after User1 assumes the existing role. Access to the S3 resources is required in addition to access to EC2 and RDS resources. question_content: Development teams in a company can create and test version-controlled IAM policies for the team's workloads. The teams will run these policies through a secure CI/CD pipeline. There are several development teams. All teams receive different degrees of access through Active Directory federation and select IAM roles.The company followed all best practices to create the IAM roles and associated policies that the company uses for Active Directory federation.A security team needs to ensure that the developers do not have the ability to grant themselves additional unapproved access to the IAM roles that the developers use or create during development.Which solution will meet this requirement?

For more information about IAM policy conditions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_elements_condition.html"IAM JSON Policy Elements: Condition.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use IAM permissions boundaries for the federated roles that the developers use.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. You can apply IAM permission boundaries to the role. Permission boundaries will create a maximum permission that the IAM role can use. If a policy is added or modified for the role, the permission boundary ensures that no actions beyond the permission boundary are permitted.For more information about IAM permission boundaries, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_boundaries.html"Permissions Boundaries for IAM Entities.For more information about IAM policy evaluation logic, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic.html"Policy Evaluation Logic.

However, this approach will not effectively control the maximum permissions for a specific role within the account. When many teams use various roles, maximum permissions will likely vary from role to role.For more information about SCPs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html"Service Control Policies (SCPs).

answer_choices.choice_content: Use IAM session policies for the roles to implement the desired controls.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. You can inject a session policy inline at the time a user assumes a role. You cannot apply session policies to the IAM role as a whole. Although you can use session policies to protect the session actions, the session policies will not affect everyone who uses the specified IAM role. Session policies affect only the specific session. A developer who has the ability to create and apply policies could apply a policy to a role. Then other developers who use that role could gain unapproved access. To prevent this scenario, you should apply a boundary to the IAM role itself.For more information about IAM session policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html#policies_session"Session Policies.

question_content: A company has an AWS account named AccountA. An independent internal audit department of the company is performing a series of audits. An inline policy for Auditor-Alan in AccountB does not prevent Auditor-Bob from assuming the S3Audit role.For more information about inline policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_managed-vs-inline.html"Managed Policies and Inline Policies.

answer_choices.choice_content: Modify the trust relationship to the S3Audit role to have the following principal:span style='font-family: "Courier New";' "arn:aws:iam::{AccountB}:user/Auditor-Alice"./span

You would improve the security posture by restricting the default trust policy to the authorized users. In this case, the trust policy for the S3Audit role allows only IAM user Auditor-Alice in AccountB to assume the role.For more information about how to provide access to an IAM user in another account, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_aws-accounts.html"Providing Access to an IAM User in Another AWS Account that You Own.For more information about how to create a role for an IAM user, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-user.html"Creating a Role to Delegate Permissions to an IAM User.

For a cross-account IAM role, the default trust policy gives all users in the other account the ability to assume the role. In this case, the trust policy of the S3Audit role allows any IAM user that begins with Auditor-A in AccountB to assume the role. This solution is not the most secure because of the unintended access.For more information about how to create a role for an IAM user, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-user.html"Creating a Role to Delegate Permissions to an IAM User.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create the S3Audit role in AccountB, and ensure that the Auditor-Alice IAM user can assume the role.

question_content: A company has an application that runs on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that consists of 25 Windows-based Amazon EC2 instances. question_content: A company has many Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes in a single AWS Region. question_content: A company runs an application across multiple Amazon EC2 instances. A new compliance requirement specifies that the application must encrypt all data. The encryption solution must rotate the encryption key every 30 days.Which solution will meet these requirements?

You cannot activate or deactivate key rotation for AWS managed keys.For more information about KMS key rotation, see ua target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/concepts.html#key-mgmt"Customer Keys and AWS Keys/a/u.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use an alias that targets a customer managed key. Configure automatic key rotation with a 30-day interval.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use an alias that targets a customer managed key. Create a new key every 30 days and update the alias.
