question_content: A company has an application hosted in an Amazon EC2 instance and wants the application to access secure strings stored in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. When the application tries to access the secure string key value, it fails. Which factors could be the cause of this failure? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: The EC2 instance role does not have decrypt permissions on the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key used to encrypt the secret.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. For the application to decrypt a secure string parameter stored in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, the EC2 instance role needs decrypt permissions to KMS.For more information about how AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store uses AWS KMS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/services-parameter-store.html"How AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store Uses AWS KMS.

answer_choices.choice_content: The EC2 instance role does not have read permissions to read the parameters in Parameter Store.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. The EC2 instance needs read permissions to the secrets in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to successfully access the secure string.For more information about AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/services-parameter-store.html#parameter-store-policies"Setting Permissions to Encrypt and Decrypt Parameter Values.

answer_choices.choice_content: Parameter Store does not have permission to use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to decrypt the parameter.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Parameter Store does not require AWS KMS permissions because it is not the service that is used to decrypt the secret. The service is not acting as an IAM principal. A principal is a workload or an individual that can make a request for operations or actions on an AWS resource.For more information about principals in IAM, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/intro-structure.html"How IAM Works.

answer_choices.choice_content: The EC2 instance role does not have encrypt permissions on the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key associated with the secret.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Because the application tries to access secure strings, the EC2 instance role in this scenario needs decrypt permissions, not encrypt permissions.For more information about how AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store uses AWS KMS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/services-parameter-store.html"How AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store Uses AWS KMS.

answer_choices.choice_content: The EC2 instance does not have any tags associated.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Although you can optionally choose to use tags for access control, simply not applying tags would not cause errors. EC2 instance tags are commonly used to classify your instances in a variety of ways in addition to access control, which includes purpose, environment, patch-group, or owner.For more information about EC2 tags, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Using_Tags.html"Tag Your Amazon EC2 Resources.

question_content: A company uses an organization in AWS Organizations to manage many AWS accounts. A security team has defined custom security controls in an AWS CloudFormation template. The security team must deploy the custom security controls to all accounts that belong to specific OUs in the organization.Which solution will meet these requirements and follow AWS security best practices?

answer_choices.choice_content: Upload the CloudFormation template to an Amazon S3 bucket that is in the security team’s account. Grant access to the template for the account administrators of each of the accounts of the appropriate OUs. Ensure the account administrators in each account use CloudFormation to deploy the custom security controls.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A solution that uses individual account administrators to deploy stacks requires more implementation effort because the security team needs to ensure the stacks are deployed. Additionally, subsequent changes to the template will require more effort. This solution will not guarantee compliance because these stacks can be deleted independently. AWS recommends that you configure services and resources centrally.For more information about CloudFormation templates, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/cfn-using-console-create-stack-template.html"Selecting a Stack Template.

answer_choices.choice_content: Enable trusted access within the organization for CloudFormation StackSets. Grant restricted access to the management account for the security team. Use CloudFormation StackSets in the management account to deploy the custom security controls as stacks to the appropriate OUs.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. AWS recommends that you use the management account and the users and roles of the management account only for tasks that can be performed only by the management account. Otherwise, AWS recommends that you configure services and resources centrally.For more information about management account best practices, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_best-practices_mgmt-acct.html"Best Practices for the Management Account.For more information about security recommendations, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/aws-account-management-and-separation.html"AWS Account Management and Separation.

answer_choices.choice_content: Enable trusted access within the organization for CloudFormation StackSets. Register a security account as a delegated administrator for StackSets. Use stack sets in the security account to deploy the custom security controls as stacks to the appropriate OUs.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. StackSets gives users the ability to create, update, or delete stacks across multiple accounts and AWS Regions with a single operation. You can delegate this feature to a specific administrator account to simplify the implementation. You can reduce the effort further by enabling trusted access within the management account. AWS recommends that you configure services and resources centrally by delegating administration features of security services to separate the accounts from the organizational billing (management) account.For more information about StackSets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/what-is-cfnstacksets.html"Working with AWS CloudFormation StackSets.For more information about how to delegate StackSets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-orgs-delegated-admin.html"Register a Delegated Administrator.For more information about enable trusted access for StackSets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-orgs-enable-trusted-access.html"Enable Trusted Access with AWS Organizations.For more information about security recommendations, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/aws-account-management-and-separation.html"AWS Account Management and Separation.

answer_choices.choice_content: Grant self-managed permissions between a security account and the organization's member accounts. Use an administration IAM role in the security account and an execution IAM role in each member account. Use CloudFormation StackSets in the security account to deploy the custom security controls as stacks to the appropriate OUs.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. StackSets gives users the ability to create, update, or delete stacks across multiple accounts and AWS Regions with a single operation. You can grant self-managed permissions to the security account (administrator account) to perform StackSets operations. However, this process is labor intensive because it requires the creation of appropriate roles in the security account and each member account. Instead, AWS strongly recommends that you use trusted access to simplify the implementation.For more information about how to grant self-managed permissions with StackSets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-prereqs-self-managed.html"Grant Self-Managed Permissions.For more information about how to use Organizations to configure AWS services, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_integrate_services.html"Using AWS Organizations with other AWS Services.

question_content: A company has approved an enterprise-wide tagging strategy to be implemented across thousands of accounts. All accounts have been migrated to AWS Organizations. Given that tags will be used to facilitate security and access, management has concerns about tag immutability and enforcement. A security engineer must develop a solution for tag enforcement at scale.Which solution should the security engineer recommend?

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a custom AWS Config rule to monitor for specific tags and prevent resource instantiation if approved tags are not present.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. AWS Config is an auditing tool. AWS Config rules can flag non-compliant resources, but cannot enforce resource tagging. In this scenario, tag policies and SCPs must be used to enforce resource tagging at scale.For more information about AWS Config, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/WhatIsConfig.html"What Is AWS Config?

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure tag policies and use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share to all accounts.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Tag policies are not a resource shared by AWS RAM. Tags can be applied to a resource share, but cannot be applied to the resources in the resource share.For more information about AWS Resource Access Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/getting-started-sharing.html"Sharing Your AWS Resources.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use the Resource Groups Tagging API to implement tags across accounts.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Resource groups tagging API allows for programmatic access to tagging functions of AWS resources. However, it does not enforce the tagging of resources.For more information about how to use the resource groups tagging API, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/resourcegroupstagging/latest/APIReference/overview.html"AWS Resource Groups Tagging API Reference.

answer_choices.choice_content: Configure tag policies at the organizational level and create resource creation request guardrails using SCPs.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. Tag policies offer centralized tag management at scale, and are integrated with AWS Organizations. Tag policies should be used in conjunction with resource request guardrails because some services still do not support tags.For more information about tag policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_tag-policies.html"Tag Policies.For more information about how to use an SCP to block the creation of resources that are missing tag keys, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html"Service Control Policies (SCPs).

question_content: A large company organizes hundreds of AWS accounts in AWS Organizations with Developer, Test, and Production OUs. Developers use the accounts in the Developer OU. Developers have full administrative privileges in their respective accounts. The company wants to allow only certain Amazon EC2 instance types to be used within the Developer OU. Because the instances are not production-level instances, auto scaling is not required for instances in the Developer OU.pHow can the company prevent developer accounts from launching unapproved EC2 instance types?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a new launch template in each AWS account in the Developer OU to deny the ec2:RunInstances API call for instance types that are not in an approved list. Associate these templates with all IAM principals in the account.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. You can only use launch templates to launch instances in Auto Scaling groups. You can use a launch template to prevent the use of certain instance types. However, you cannot attach a launch template to an OU. You would need an SCP to restrict the launch of specific instance types for an OU.For more information about launch templates, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/use-launch-templates-to-control-launching-instances.html"Use Launch Templates to Control Launching Instances.For more information about SCPs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html"Service Control Policies (SCPs).

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an IAM policy to deny the ec2:RunInstances API call for instance types that are not in an approved list. Attach the policy to all IAM principals in all the AWS accounts in the Developer OU.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Because the developers have full administrative privileges in their accounts, any developer could remove an attached IAM policy that denies the ec2:RunInstances API call. For more information about the privileges an AWS user has within managed policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_job-functions.html"AWS Managed Policies for Job Functions.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use a managed SCP that is attached to the organization's root account to deny the ec2:RunInstances API call for instance types that are not in an approved list.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A solution that attaches an SCP to the organization's root account would prevent all accounts in all OUs from launching certain instance types. In this scenario, the Developer, Test, and Production OUs would all be impacted. SCPs are inherited through a well-defined hierarchy that starts at the organization's root and flows out to all OUs. To prevent the launch of certain instance types at the OU level, you must attach an SCP to the specific OU where the company wants to enforce the policy. In this scenario, you should only apply the SCP to the Developer OU.For more information about the effects of inheritance on SCPs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_inheritance_auth.html"Inheritance for Service Control Policies.For more information about the effects of SCPs on root accounts, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html#scp-warning-testing-effect"Testing Effects of SCPs.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an SCP to deny the ec2:RunInstances API call for instance types that are not in an approved list. Attach the policy to the Developer OU.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. SCPs provide an overarching guardrail for IAM identities within the attached OU. You can use SCPs to prevent the launch of certain instance types.For more information about the use of SCPs to prevent the launch of certain instance types, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_examples.html#examples_ec2"Example Service Control Policies.For more information about SCPs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html"Service Control Policies (SCPs).

question_content: A company is migrating its existing infrastructure to AWS. The company has set up an organization in AWS Organizations. Each of the company's development teams has its own AWS account. The company wants to give the developers the ability to deploy a range of different services securely. However, the company does not want to provide full administrative access to each team. The company’s security team also needs to have visibility into what is deployed in each account.Which solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: Designate the security team’s account as a delegated administrator for AWS Service Catalog. Develop products for common services that the development teams use. Use a launch constraint on the products to minimize IAM permissions. Allow developers to deploy from AWS Service Catalog. Use the AWS Service Catalog console to inspect what the developers have deployed.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. AWS Service Catalog gives users the ability to create and manage catalogs of IT services that are approved for AWS. These IT services can include everything from VM images, servers, software, and databases to complete multi-tier application architectures. End users can quickly deploy only the approved IT services that are necessary. The end user must follow the constraints the company has set.A launch constraint specifies the IAM role that AWS Service Catalog assumes when an end user launches a product. This configuration will allow developers to launch products from the AWS Service Catalog without the need to grant developers permissions to the underlying services that are deployed.This solution meets the requirements because the security team can centrally manage the AWS Service Catalog as a delegated administrator in the organization with visibility from the AWS Service Catalog console.For more information about AWS Service Catalog, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/adminguide/introduction.html"What Is AWS Service Catalog?For more information about AWS Service Catalog launch constraints, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/adminguide/constraints-launch.html"AWS Service Catalog Launch Constraints.

answer_choices.choice_content: Designate the security team’s account as a delegated administrator for AWS CloudFormation StackSets. Develop CloudFormation templates for common services that the development teams use. Apply an SCP to the developers' accounts to minimize IAM permissions. Allow developers to deploy from StackSets. Use the CloudFormation console to inspect what the developers have deployed.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. StackSets extends the capability of stacks because it gives users the ability to create, update, or delete stacks across multiple accounts and AWS Regions with a single operation. You can use an administrator account to define, manage, and use a  CloudFormation template as the basis for provisioning stacks into target accounts across specified Regions.The delegated administrator is the only account that is allowed to use StackSets to deploy to specific OUs or individual accounts. Developer accounts will not be able to access the service to deploy any centrally managed CloudFormation templates. SCPs are a type of Organization policy that can be used to manage permissions in an Organization. SCPs offer central control over the maximum available permissions for all accounts in an Organization. SCPs help to ensure accounts stay within an Organization’s access control guidelines. Although SCPs are a good way to restrict maximum permissions to accounts within an Organization, this approach does not meet the requirements.For more information about StackSets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/what-is-cfnstacksets.html"Working with AWS CloudFormation StackSets.For more information about SCPs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html"Service Control Policies (SCPs).

answer_choices.choice_content: Use the security team’s account to create an EC2 Image Builder image that will create an AMI image pipeline. Develop recipes for common services that the development teams use. Minimize IAM permissions by allowing developers to launch instances only by using the security team’s AMIs. Use the AWS Billing and Cost Management console to inspect usage of the AMIs that are deployed in each account.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Image Builder is a fully managed AWS service that gives you the ability to to automate the creation, management, and deployment of customized, secure, and up-to-date AMIs that are preinstalled and preconfigured with software and settings to meet specific IT standards.You can create images from the security team’s account and share the images with accounts or OUs within an organization. However, AMIs will limit the services you can deploy to services that are created within Amazon EC2. The development teams would likely want to use other services, including databases, serverless services, and storage. This solution would not make these services available.For more information about Image Builder, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/what-is-image-builder.html"What Is EC2 Image Builder?

answer_choices.choice_content: Use the security team’s account to create a private marketplace in AWS Marketplace. Select AWS Marketplace products for common services that the development teams use. Attach only the AWSPrivateMarketplaceAdminFullAccess policy to users in the development accounts to minimize IAM permissions. Use the AWS Marketplace console to inspect usage of subscriptions.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. A private marketplace determines which products users in an AWS account, such as business users and engineering teams, can procure from AWS Marketplace. You build a private marketplace on top of AWS Marketplace. A private marketplace gives administrators the ability to create and customize curated digital catalogs of approved independent software vendors (ISVs) and products that conform to the company's in-house policies.However, the AWSPrivateMarketplaceAdminFullAccess policy is the permission that is necessary to set up and configure a private marketplace. You should not grant this permission to developers within the organization. If you assign this policy to developers, the developers would have full access to select any products as well as the potential to delete the private marketplace entirely. The AWSMarketplaceManageSubscriptions policy would be more appropriate for the developers in this scenario. For more information about AWS Marketplace, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/buyerguide/what-is-marketplace.html"What Is AWS Marketplace?For more information about private marketplaces, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/buyerguide/private-marketplace.html"Private Marketplaces.For more information about how to control access to AWS Marketplace, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/buyerguide/buyer-iam-users-groups-policies.html"Controlling Access to AWS Marketplace Subscriptions.

question_content: A company is setting up products to deploy in AWS Service Catalog. Management is concerned that when users launch products, elevated IAM privileges will be required to create resources.How should the company mitigate this concern?

answer_choices.choice_content: Add a template constraint to each product in the portfolio.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Service Catalog is a service used to manage catalogs of IT services that are approved by the company to deploy on AWS. Service Catalog template constraints can be used to limit the options that are available to end users when they launch a product. These template constraints also ensure that the end users can use products without breaching the compliance requirements of an organization. They do not specify the IAM role that Service Catalog assumes.For more information about template constraints, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/adminguide/catalogs_constraints_template-constraints.html"Service Catalog Template Constraints.

answer_choices.choice_content: Add a launch constraint to each product in the portfolio.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. Service Catalog is a service used to manage catalogs of IT services that are approved by the company to deploy on AWS. Service Catalog launch constraints specify the IAM role that Service Catalog assumes when an end user launches, updates, or terminates a product. These launch constraints are used to assign a role to the portfolio so that the individual user does not need additional privileges to create resources.For more information about launch constraints, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/adminguide/constraints-launch.html"Service Catalog Launch Constraints.

answer_choices.choice_content: Define resource update constraints for each product in the portfolio.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Service Catalog is a service used to manage catalogs of IT services that are approved by the company to deploy on AWS. Service Catalog tag update constraints are used to allow or disallow end users to update tags on resources. They do not specify the IAM role that Service Catalog assumes.For more information about tag update constraints, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/adminguide/constraints-resourceupdate.html"Service Catalog Tag Update Constraints.

answer_choices.choice_content: Update the AWS CloudFormation template backing the product to include a service role configuration.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. This is a feasible option, but only if the resources are deployed from CloudFormation directly, not through the use of Service Catalog. Service Catalog does not expose this feature of CloudFormation, nor would updating the CloudFormation template provide this functionality. This update is done at the time of the API call to CloudFormation.For more information about service role configuration in CloudFormation, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-iam-servicerole.html"AWS CloudFormation Service Role.For more information about how to set CloudFormation stack options, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/cfn-console-add-tags.html"Setting AWS CloudFormation Stack Options.

question_content: A company has an unencrypted Amazon S3 bucket that contains millions of objects. Some objects contain customer information such as personal identifiable information (PII) and customer account numbers. Multiple applications access these objects.A security engineer must provide a report to the company's senior management that identifies any sensitive data. The security engineer must also ensure that all current and future objects are encrypted.Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?

answer_choices.choice_content: Run an Amazon Macie discovery job by using appropriate managed data identifiers. Review Macie findings to generate a report. Create a new S3 bucket that uses default encryption. Use AWS CLI to transfer the objects to the new bucket. Update the applications to access the new bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: div class="aws-rationale-content"pIncorrect. Macie automates the discovery of sensitive data. To discover custom-defined sensitive data types such as customer account numbers, you must create and apply a custom data identifier to the Macie discovery job. This option does not meet the data discovery requirement. This option does meet the encryption requirements. However, a solution that creates new encrypted bucket, transfers the objects, and updates the applications to point to the new bucket will require more implementation effort than necessary.

question_content: A company mandates that all its Amazon S3 buckets must be encrypted with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys. A security consultant wants to receive an email notification each time an S3 bucket becomes noncompliant. The email notification must contain the noncompliant S3 bucket's name, the AWS Region that the S3 bucket is in, and the time at which the S3 bucket became noncompliant.pThe company has activated AWS Security Hub and AWS Config for the account. The security consultant sets up an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic and subscribes the relevant email account to the topic.pWhich combination of steps should the security consultant take next to meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)/p/div

answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. The AWS Config managed rule, s3-default-encryption-kms, does not allow you to set a frequency for the rule to run. The rule only runs when a resource's configuration changes. The rule cannot be configured to run every hour.For more information about AWS Config, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/s3-default-encryption-kms.html" tabindex="-1"s3-default-encryption-kms.

answer_choices.choice_content: In AWS Config, add the s3-default-encryption-kms managed rule to the list of enforced rules. Set the rule to run when an S3 bucket is created or edited.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. The AWS Config managed rule, s3-default-encryption-kms, verifies whether the S3 buckets are encrypted with AWS KMS. The S3 bucket would be identified as NON_COMPLIANT if it is not encrypted with an AWS KMS key. The rule would run whenever the resource configuration changes. In this case, that is when an S3 bucket is created, edited, or deleted.For more information about S3 event notifications, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/s3-default-encryption-kms.html" tabindex="-1"s3-default-encryption-kms.

question_content: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage 50 AWS accounts. A security team notified an account administrator of data exfiltration activities by some Amazon EC2 instances that are in a member account. The account administrator immediately took the appropriate actions. When the security team reviewed further, the team discovered that Amazon EC2 service had an increased expenditure due to this incident.pThe security team must identify similar expenditure fluctuations in each member account so account administrators can take immediate action to resolve similar security incidents.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?/p/div

A cost monitor can analyze all AWS services independently or by member accounts, cost allocation tags, or cost categories. The team can create alert subscriptions to receive alerts individually or as an aggregated daily summary. A daily summary sends one daily email that contains multiple anomalies that occurred during that day. However, this summary will not notify the account administrator immediately, and the account administrator will not be able to respond to security incidents quickly. To notify the account administrator more quickly, the team should configure individual alerts.

question_content: A team of developers is working on a prototype that includes multiple web services that run as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services behind a publicly accessible Application Load Balancer (ALB). The developers deployed the services in private subnets. The services need to be frequently updated. The services require indirect internet access for the updates. Additionally, the services must have the ability to communicate internally among each other. During the prototype development, AWS Cost Explorer forecasted unexpected costs for the next three months. The developers discovered that the usage of NAT gateways had unexpectedly increased in the previous month. A system administrator must attribute cost to this usage and resolve any root cause.Which combination of actions should the system administrator take to identify and resolve the security gap? (Select THREE.)

answer_choices.choice_content: Use Cost Explorer to view the cost data for the previous month. Group by service and usage type. Check for any unusual costs.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. Cost Explorer is a tool that gives you the ability to view and analyze costs and usage. Cost Explorer has a default report that provides a detailed breakdown for all services in a tabular view. The system administrator can use this report to determine which services generate unexpected costs in the previous month. You can confirm that the unexpected data transfer costs are a result of NAT gateway use if you group and filter the cost data by using filters such asEC2: NAT Gateway - Data Processed orEC2: Data Transfer-Internet (Out).For more information about Cost Explorer, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/ce-what-is.html"Analyzing Your Costs with AWS Cost Explorer.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create an AWS services monitor type in AWS Cost Anomaly Detection. Create an alert subscription that has a cost threshold.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Cost Anomaly Detection is an AWS Cost Management feature that uses machine learning to continuously monitor cost and usage to detect unusual spends. AWS services cost monitor type evaluates all AWS services that an AWS account uses for anomalies. You can configure alert notifications for the detection of unexpected spends in an account. This solution would help detect any future unexpected costs from NAT gateways as an anomaly. However, this solution would not provide information about the past usage and will not help attribute the cost of NAT gateways usage in the previous month.For more information about Cost Anomaly Detection, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/manage-ad.html"Detecting Unusual Spend with AWS Cost Anomaly Detection.

answer_choices.choice_content: Turn on VPC Flow Logs for the VPC where the ECS cluster is located with an Amazon S3 bucket as the destination. Use Amazon Athena to analyze the flow logs for any traffic that uses NAT gateways.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. VPC Flow Logs is a feature that captures information about the IP traffic to and from network interfaces in a VPC. You can publish flow log data to Amazon CloudWatch Logs or Amazon S3. You can use Athena to analyze the flow logs in an S3 bucket. After you attribute the cost to the NAT gateway usage, the flow logs will help determine which VPC resources are sending the traffic to the NAT gateways and what the destinations are for such traffic. The flow logs will identify that in addition to using the ALB's endpoint for communication between each other, the web services are using NAT gateways to send communications across the internet. This communication must be internal to improve the security posture.For more information about VPC Flow Logs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html"Logging IP Traffic Using VPC Flow Logs.

answer_choices.choice_content: Use VPC Reachability Analyzer to create and analyze paths between the network interfaces of the web services. Review the traffic paths that use NAT gateways.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. Reachability Analyzer tests connectivity between a source and a destination in a VPC. Reachability Analyzer produces hop-by-hop details of the virtual network path between the source and the reachable destination. When the destination is not reachable, Reachability Analyzer identifies the component within the VPC that is blocking the connection. Reachability Analyzer does not track the traffic outside the VPC. Reachability Analyzer will not detect that a web service uses a NAT gateway to connect to the internet and reaches out to another web service by using the ALB's public endpoint. Reachability Analyzer would provide a Not Reachable status with no reason. This solution does not help to determine whether NAT gateways are used in the path.For more information about Reachability Analyzer, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/reachability/what-is-reachability-analyzer.html"What Is VPC Reachability Analyzer?

answer_choices.choice_content: Update the web services to use the existing ALB’s private DNS endpoint for internal communications between the services.
answer_choices.solution_content: Incorrect. After you determine that the web services are using NAT gateways to communicate with each other and are unintentionally communicating through the internet, you can resolve the security gap by using private IP addresses to redirect this communication internally. However, the public ALB has a single endpoint that resolves to the public IP addresses of the load balancer's nodes, not the private IP address.For more information about load balancer scheme, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/userguide/how-elastic-load-balancing-works.html#load-balancer-scheme"Load Balancer Scheme.

answer_choices.choice_content: Create a new internal ALB. Register and update the web services to use the newly-created internal ALB for internal communications between the services.
answer_choices.solution_content: Correct. After you determine that the web services are using NAT gateways to communicate with each other and are unintentionally communicating through the internet, you can resolve the security gap by using private IP addresses to redirect this communication internally. The nodes of an internal load balancer have only private IP addresses. The internal load balancer's endpoint resolves to the private IP addresses of the nodes. Therefore, the web services can internally access the load balancer. Lastly, the internal load balancer uses private IP addresses to route requests to the targets. When you register the web services ECS task to the load balancer, the web services can internally communicate with one another without the use of NAT gateways.For more information about load balancer scheme, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/userguide/how-elastic-load-balancing-works.html#load-balancer-scheme"Load Balancer Scheme.
